questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn by turning only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: You can see through vehicles ahead to check traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space to stop on a slippery road. Keep at least a four-second distance behind other vehicles if the road is slippery, if you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy and someone might cut in front of you.

questions.question: When wearing a protective jacket in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool down.
Remove the jacket to stay cool in the sun.
Keep the jacket on for protection and to prevent overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on for protection and to prevent overheating.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. In hot weather, it also helps prevent dehydration. Most motorcycle jackets are designed to keep riders from getting too hot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to signal the other vehicle to proceed.
Go through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Proceed through the intersection with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow has the same meaning as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Reduce the risk of a crash at night by riding slower and staying farther back from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, press gently on the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward.

questions.question: Before you start riding, the fuel valve should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Always open the fuel valve before starting your ride. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines from before, but it will stop running once that fuel runs out.

questions.question: To make a quick turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your motorcycle quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, lean your motorcycle in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more you must lean.

questions.question: Service signs are what color and have what letters?
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When shifting gears in a curve, you should:

options.text: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
Shift in the curve instead of before it.
Shift in the curve to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only shift if you can do it smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in engine power can cause your rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: Under normal riding conditions, the best way to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on. Use your high beam during the day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle moves.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you approach an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up as it gets close.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up as it gets close.
questions.explanation: If you see a dog approaching, slow down and downshift until it gets close. Then quickly accelerate away from the dog.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.
Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you complete a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after finishing a turn or lane change. Leaving it on can confuse other drivers.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride right behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, position yourself so the driver can see you in:
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror, where they look most often.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, you should return to your lane when:

options.text: You can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
You feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your original lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down at the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of the lane when passing parked cars. This position helps you avoid car doors opening, people stepping out, and cars pulling into the road. Be ready to change position if conditions change.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip.
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is usually on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: When is a motorcyclist easiest to see by other drivers?

options.text: Riding on the right side of the lane
Riding in the center of the lane
Riding on the left side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best for a motorcyclist following a car. This position shows up in the driver's rearview mirror. Be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.
